title: Motor Overload Shutdown
shortDescription: Disposal motor has tripped its thermal overload protector.
fullDescription:
LG disposals include a thermal overload that cuts power when the motor overheats or draws too much current. Overloads typically result from jams or extended grinding of tough scraps.

Allow the unit to cool, clear any jam, and press the reset button on the bottom.

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off wall switch before inspecting.

fixSteps.title: Clear jam
fixSteps.instruction: Use an Allen wrench in the bottom port to rotate the motor shaft and free the jam.

fixSteps.title: Press reset
fixSteps.instruction: After 10 minutes cooling, press the red reset button on the bottom of the unit.

whenToCallPro: If the reset button does not stay pressed or motor hums without turning.
videoSearchQuery: LG garbage disposal reset button overload

faq.a: Usually a small bone or utensil inside; inspect with a flashlight.

title: Grinding Chamber Jammed
shortDescription: Disposal will not turn - foreign object stuck.
fullDescription:
The motor hums but impellers do not spin, indicating a jam. Bones, fruit pits, silverware, or fibrous food can block the grinding plate.

Never put hands in the disposal; use the wrench port or pliers.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power at the switch or breaker.

fixSteps.title: Free impellers
fixSteps.instruction: Insert Allen wrench into bottom port and rotate until free.

fixSteps.title: Remove debris
fixSteps.instruction: Use long pliers or tongs to remove foreign object from top.

whenToCallPro: If the shaft will not rotate even with the wrench.

faq.a: Absolutely not - always use tools and cut power first.

title: Water Leaking from Disposal
shortDescription: Disposal is leaking from sink flange, side inlet, or body.
fullDescription:
Leaks commonly occur at three points: the mounting flange under the sink, the dishwasher inlet, and the discharge pipe. In rare cases, the disposal body itself cracks and requires replacement.

Identify the leak source before acting.

fixSteps.title: Identify leak
fixSteps.instruction: Dry all joints and run water to find the leak origin.

fixSteps.title: Tighten or reseal
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten mounting ring or replace plumber's putty at sink flange.

whenToCallPro: If the disposal body itself is leaking - replacement needed.

faq.q: Can I ignore a small leak?
faq.a: No - water damages cabinetry and can cause mold.

title: Unusual Grinding or Rattling Noise
shortDescription: Disposal is louder than normal, indicating potential damage.
fullDescription:
A loud rattle usually means a foreign object in the chamber. A metallic scraping noise can indicate worn impellers or a loose grind plate.

Inspect immediately to prevent further damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect with light
fixSteps.instruction: Shine a flashlight down and remove any object with tongs.

whenToCallPro: If noise persists after clearing, impellers may need replacement.

faq.a: Yes - a loose object can damage the grind plate or fly out.

title: Disposal Draining Slowly
shortDescription: Water backs up in sink during disposal use.
fullDescription:
Slow draining typically means a clog in the p-trap or discharge line. Do not use chemical drain cleaners in a disposal.

Disassemble the trap manually to clear.

fixSteps.title: Remove p-trap
fixSteps.instruction: Place bucket, loosen slip nuts, clean trap.

whenToCallPro: If clog is downstream of visible plumbing.

faq.a: No - chemicals can damage seals and remain a hazard.

title: Disposal Not Receiving Power
fullDescription:
No sound at all - not even a hum - indicates a power supply issue. Check the reset button first, then breaker and switch.

Verify 120V at the disposal before assuming motor failure.

fixSteps.title: Press reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press the red reset button on the bottom.

fixSteps.title: Test voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Use multimeter at disposal wire nuts.

whenToCallPro: If voltage is present but motor does not run.
videoSearchQuery: LG garbage disposal no power fix

faq.a: Yes, LG places the reset button centrally on the bottom.

title: Motor Burning Smell
fullDescription:
A burning odor indicates the motor windings are overheating or have failed. Continuing to run the unit risks fire.

Power off immediately and plan for replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace unit
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new disposal - motor repair is not practical.

whenToCallPro: If you have not replaced a disposal before - plumbing work is involved.

title: Dishwasher Backing into Sink
shortDescription: Dirty dishwasher water drains into the sink via disposal.
fullDescription:
If the dishwasher drain line feeds the disposal and the knockout plug was not removed, or the disposal is clogged, water can back up during a dishwasher cycle.

Clear the disposal, check the air gap, and inspect the drain hose.
symptoms: Water in sink after dishwasher cycle

fixSteps.title: Remove knockout
fixSteps.instruction: Use a screwdriver and hammer to remove the dishwasher inlet knockout if this is a new install.

fixSteps.title: Clear discharge
fixSteps.instruction: Run disposal with water to flush any residual food.

whenToCallPro: If plumbing beyond the disposal is clogged.

faq.q: Do all new disposals need the plug removed?
faq.a: Only if connected to a dishwasher - otherwise leave it in place.
